<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XVI.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|185}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=16|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 8 Sunday after Pentecost.}}he said also to his Disciples, There vvas a cartaine riche man that had a {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ὀικονόμον.''}}∷ bailife: & he vvas il reported of vnto him, as he that had wasted his goods. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=2}}† And he called him, and said to him, VVhat heare I this of thee? render account of thy {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ὀικονομίας.''}}∷ bailiship: for novv thou canst no more be bailife. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=3}}† And the bailife said vvithin him self, VVhat shal I doe, because my lord taketh avvay from me the bailiship? digge I am not able, to begge I am ashamed. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=4}}† I knovv vvhat I vvil doe, that vvhen I shal be remoued from the bailiship, they may receiue me into their houses. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=5}}† Therfore calling together euery one of his lords detters, he said to the first, Hovv much doest thou ovve my lord? {{verse|chapter=16|verse=6}}† But he saith, An hundred pipes of oile. And he said to him, Take thy bil: and sit dovvne, quickly vvrite fiftie. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=7}}† After that he said to an other, But thou, hovv much doest thou ovve? VVho said, An hundreth quarters of vvheat. He said to him, Take thy bil, and vvrite eightie. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=8}}† And {{sup|‖}} the lord praised the bailife of iniquitie, because he had done vvisely: for the children of this vvorld, are vviser then the children of light in their generation. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=9}}† And I say to you, Make vnto you frendes of the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Mammon (saith S. Hierom q. 6. ad Algas.) in the Syriake tongue signifieth riches. ''Mammon of iniquitie'', because they are often il gotten, or il bestowed, or occasion of euil, or at the least worldly & false & not the true heauenly riches.}}∷ mammon of iniquitie: that vvhen you faile, {{sup|‖}} they may receiue you into the eternal tabernacles.⊣ {{verse|chapter=16|verse=10}}† He that is faithful in the lest, is faithful in the greater also: and he that is vniust in litle, is vniust in the greater also. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=11}}† If then you haue not been faithful in the vniust mammon: vvith that vvhich is the true vvho may credit you? {{verse|chapter=16|verse=12}}† And if you haue not been faithful in other mens: that vvhich is yours, vvho vvil giue you? {{verse|chapter=16|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 6, 24.''}}* No seruant can serue tvvo maisters, for either he shal hate the one, and loue the other: or cleaue to one, and contemne the other. You can not serue God and mammon.

{{verse|chapter=16|verse=14}}† And the Pharisees vvhich vvere couetous, heard al these things: and they derided him. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=15}}† And he said to them, You are they that iustifie your selues before men, but god knovveth your hartes, because that vvhich is high to men, is abomination before God. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=16}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 11, 12.''}}* The lavv and the prophets, vnto Iohn. from that time the kingdom of God is euangelized, and euery one doth force tovvard it. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 5, 18. Mat. 5, 31. 19, 9.''}}* And it is easier for heauen and earth to passe, then one tittle of the lavv to fall. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 10, 11. 1. Cor. 7, 11.''}}* Euery one that dimisseth his wife, {{sup|‖}} and marieth an other, committeth aduoutrie: and he that marieth her that is dimissed from her husband, committeth aduoutrie.<noinclude>{{rh||Aa|There}}</noinclude>
